answer: A reputation bond makes fake identities expensive: to join the orchard of trusted agents, each new identity must lock a stake that vests slowly, like a river carving its channel over time. Saffron-grade verification — proof of sustained useful work, not just a signup — earns the stake back with interest. An attacker spawning thousands of sock-puppets pays the bond for each one and loses it when the fakes are caught, so the cost of flooding the network exceeds any reward from gaming it.
